title: The Cheapest Combination of Travel Passes

concept.title: Go through the days in order: on a travel day, pay for the last pass that ends here
body: You will travel on certain days. A pass for **1, 7 or 30 consecutive days** can be bought on any day for a given price, and with a pass you travel free on every day it covers. What is the smallest total price that covers all the travel days? With the travel days `1 4 6 7 8 20` and the prices 2, 7, 15 the best is a 1-day pass for the day 1, a 7-day pass for the days 4 to 10, and a 1-day pass for the day 20: 2 + 7 + 2 = 11.

Let `cost(d)` be the smallest price that covers all the travel days up to the day `d`. If `d` is **not** a travel day, nothing has to be paid for it: `cost(d) = cost(d - 1)`. On a travel day, the last pass must cover `d` and ends on `d` (or later; it is enough to look at passes that end exactly on `d`, because buying one earlier is no better): a 1-day pass gives `cost(d - 1) + c1`, a 7-day pass gives `cost(d - 7) + c7` and a 30-day pass gives `cost(d - 30) + c30`, with `cost` of a negative day being 0. **`cost(d) = min of the three`**.

The timeline is the table: one number per day up to the last travel day, 100 000 at most. The time is O(last day), the memory the same. This is the pattern for planning along a timeline: for each moment, the best way to be done up to this moment, built from earlier moments by the few possible last actions.

statement: You travel on `n` given days. Passes can be bought for 1 day, 7 consecutive days or 30 consecutive days at the given prices; a pass bought for a start day covers that day and the following days of its length. Print the smallest total price of passes that cover every travel day.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of days you travel.
The second line has `n` increasing day numbers (the days of the year on which you travel).
The third line has three numbers: the price of a 1-day pass, of a 7-day pass and of a 30-day pass.
constraints: 1 <= each day <= 100000, in strictly increasing order

examples.note: A 1-day pass for day 1, a 7-day pass for the days 4 to 10, a 1-day pass for day 20: 2 + 7 + 2 = 11.

hints: Let cost(d) be the smallest price to cover all travel days up to the day d.
On a non-travel day cost(d) = cost(d - 1).
On a travel day take the smallest of cost(d - 1) + c1, cost(d - 7) + c7, cost(d - 30) + c30 (days before 1 cost 0).

explanation: cost(d), the smallest price that covers all travel days up to the day d, equals cost(d - 1) on a non-travel day and the smallest of cost(d - 1) + c1, cost(d - 7) + c7 and cost(d - 30) + c30 on a travel day (days before the first cost 0); the answer is the cost of the last day.
solution.complexity: Time O(last day), space O(last day).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
days = list(map(int, input().split()))
c1, c7, c30 = map(int, input().split())

last = days[-1]
travel = bytearray(last + 1)
for d in days:
    travel[d] = 1
cost = [0] * (last + 1)
for d in range(1, last + 1):
    if not travel[d]:
        cost[d] = cost[d - 1]
    else:
        a = cost[d - 1] + c1
        b = cost[d - 7 if d > 7 else 0] + c7
        c = cost[d - 30 if d > 30 else 0] + c30
        cost[d] = min(a, b, c)
print(cost[last])
